newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arab Bank drags down Jordan bourse.
newsitem.headline: Arab Bank drags down Jordan bourse.

text.p: Jordan's bourse was dragged lower at the start of weekly trade on Saturday by investor dismay over delays at Arab Bank in setting a date of a promised bonus share, brokers said.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.56 percent to 152.86 points after shares worth 367,316 dinars ($518,807) changed hands.
Brokers said a bearish trend since last week continued to dominate investor sentiment as most investors and large institutional buyers steer away from the market, helping to drag it lower.
Arab Bank dropped 2.00 dinars to 254 dinars after the bank's chairman squashed investors' hopes at Friday's AGM of a definitive word on when the bank's board would offer a promised bonus share issue.

"Investors had expected to get a direct answer on the timing of the capitalisation and bonus share, which the bank's board linked to the ratification of the law," said Ibrahim Odeh of Wataniyah brokerage firm.
The bank's management said the timing of a bonus share was linked with formal ratification of a recently passed law cancelling a 15 percent tax on capital increases.
Shares have fallen from 269 dinars two weeks ago on fears that the bonus share issue would be indefinitely delayed.
Housing Bank, which was last week's focus of investor interest, was unchanged at 4.80 dinars.
Only a handful of mainly industrial stock saw some activity: Jordan Industrial Resources and Jordan Petroleum Refinery which both shed 0.01 dinars and 0.08 dinars respectively.
Leading blue-chip drug firms Arab Pharmaceutical Maufacturing and Arab Pharmaceutical Chemical came under selling pressure.
